claims.text: The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% each of W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr exhibits severe lattice distortion.
Atomic-size mismatch among the components causes the severe lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion alters dislocation core structures in WTaTiVZr.
Severe lattice distortion modifies dislocation core energies.
Lattice distortion raises the activation barrier for dislocation pinning.
Lattice distortion reduces dislocation drag and enhances dislocation mobility in WTaTiVZr.
Reduced dislocation drag enables more homogeneous and sustained plastic flow.
At temperatures above approximately 1000°C, WTaTiVZr should exhibit greater plastic strain than commercial pure tungsten.
At temperatures above approximately 1000°C, WTaTiVZr should exhibit greater toughness than commercial pure tungsten.
Under equivalent high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr should exhibit a more uniform distribution of plastic deformation than pure tungsten.
Under equivalent high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr should exhibit lower dislocation accumulation than pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten has a more uniform, nearly defect-free lattice without severe lattice distortion.
Pure tungsten exhibits higher dislocation drag than WTaTiVZr under equivalent high-temperature conditions.
Pure tungsten is expected to show more localized plasticity and embrittlement than WTaTiVZr under the specified loading conditions.
Suppressing nanoprecipitate formation isolates severe lattice distortion as the principal source of differences in dislocation behavior.
The proposed mechanism is applicable above approximately 1000°C when nanoprecipitate formation is suppressed.
Residual nanoprecipitates and high-temperature diffusion may also influence dislocation behavior.
